subject: spanish
title: Stamp 3: Relative Clauses and Gerundio
welcome_lead: Stamp relative clauses and the gerund in Spanish.
meta_desc: A-Level Spanish adventure on oraciones de relativo and the gerundio.

concepts.def: Relative clause introduced by que, quien, el cual, cuyo.
Most common relative pronoun, referring to people or things, subject or object.
Relative pronouns referring only to people, often after prepositions.
Whose; agreeing in gender and number with the possessed noun.
Form ending in -ando/-iendo expressing simultaneous or ongoing action.
Progressive construction: estoy hablando (I am speaking).

walkthroughs.body_html: Que: default, for things or people in defining clauses. Quien: people, especially in non-defining clauses or after prepositions. Cuyo: possessive (whose), agrees with the noun.
El hombre cuya casa es grande — The man whose house is big. Cuya agrees with casa, not with hombre.
Estaba leyendo — I was reading (progressive). Salio corriendo — He left running (manner). Estudiando se aprende — One learns by studying.
